N o . 1 1 9 4 0 o f 2 0 1 7 h a s b e e n f i l e d t o q u a s h t h e i m p u g n e d o r d e r i n L e t t e r No.L.A-1(5)/36241/2012 dated 26.10.2016 on the file of the respondent and consequently, direct the respondent to issue 'No Objection Certificate' for the purpose of construction in the petitioner's property measuring an extent of 2050 sq.ft in Plot No.35 comprised in S.No.632/1 as per Patta S.No.632/1B of Sholinganallur Village, situated in Neduncheziyan https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.11940 and 15207 of 2017 Street, Tambaram Taluk, Kancheepuram District within a time frame to be fixed by this Court.

2. W.P.No.15207 of 2017 has been filed seeking for issuance of Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents to treat the land acquisition proceedings relied on in Letter No.A-1(5)/36421/2012 dated 26.10.2016 in respect of the petitioner's plot measuring an extent of 2050 sq.ft in Plot No.35 comprised in S.No.632/1, as per Patta S.No.632/1B of Sholinganallur Village situated in Neduncheziyan Street, Tambaram Taluk, Kancheepuram District as lapsed in view of Section 24(2)
of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
3.

It is the claim of the petitioner that he purchased the subject property from one B.Muthulakshmi by virtue of a registered Sale Deed dated 21.12.2006 vide Doc.No.7333 of 2006 on the file of the SRO, Neelangarai.

Further, the subject property with larger extent of adjoining properties were sought to be acquired for forming neighborhood Housing https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.11940 and 15207 of 2017 Colony by the Government through the Tamil Nadu Housing Board vide a notification dated 23.05.1990 G.O.Ms.No.454 Housing and Urban Development Department under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act
, subsequently, a declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act was also issued, vide G.O.Ms.No.996, Housing and Urban Development Department, dated 17.06.1991.
Challenging the same, the plot owners filed W.P.Nos.10240 of 1991 etc., before this Court.
This Court, by order dated 24.1.1996, quashed the entire acquisition proceedings covered by two layouts.
In the said judgment, this Court has recorded factual findings pertaining to location of layout on the fringe of the proposed scheme and also other relevant factors for quashing the proceedings.
The further claim of the petitioner is that his vendor purchased the subject property, even before the proposed acquisition.
The petitioner is the subsequent purchaser and he purchased the said property on 21.12.2006, i.e. after quashing of acquisition proceedings by the Division Bench of this Court.

4. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Tamil Nadu Housing Board submitted that already acquisition proceedings completed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.11940 and 15207 of 2017 and Award has been passed.
Based on the Award, the amount was deposited in the Civil Court.

Reference also taken on file in L.A.O.P.No.156 of 1995 and possession also taken over Felix M.Cruz vs The Tamil Nadu Housing Board on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108724868/
3 from the owner of the property.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The writ petitioner is the subsequent purchaser after quashing of acquisition proceedings and hence, he is not entitled to the relief sought for in this writ petition.

5. When the matter was taken up for hearing, this Court directed the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Tamil Nadu Housing Board to produce the document to prove as to whether the Award amount has been deposited in the Civil Court.

6. Today, when the matter is taken up for hearing, the learned Standing counsel produced a copy of the Register, which clearly shows that the Award was passed in the year 1993 vide Award No.2/1993 and the amount also deposited vide L.A.O.P.No.156 of 1995 on 15.02.1994 itself before the competent Tribunal.

Further, the then land owner handed over the possession to the Government and hence, the petitioner, who is none https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.11940 and 15207 of 2017 other than the subsequent purchaser, is not entitled to get the relief as sought for in these writ petitions as he purchased the property on 21.12.2016 which is earlier to his sale and completion of all proceedings.
7. Accordingly, these Writ Petitions are dismissed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
There shall be no order as to costs.
